title: Electrical quantities in operational context
summary: Refresh voltage, current, impedance, power, apparent power, power factor, energy and frequency, then connect each directly to equipment ratings, loading, fault behaviour and source compatibility.

title: AC, DC and three-phase systems
summary: Re-establish AC/DC and three-phase relationships before applying them to rectifiers, DC links, batteries, inverters, phase sequence and source transfer.

title: The data-centre power chain
summary: Trace a generic facility from incoming supply through HV distribution, transformers, LV switchboards, resilient paths, critical power conversion and downstream loads.

title: Reading professional SLDs
summary: Interpret device symbols, normal states, tags, ratings, drawing continuations, bus sections, incomers, couplers and system boundaries.

title: Architecture reconstruction
summary: Rebuild a complex fictional SLD in layers and explain what each new layer changes about energisation, redundancy and operational control.

title: Hazard and energy recognition
summary: Separate electrical hazard, source identification, stored energy and equipment state from assumptions based on normal running arrangements.

title: Roles, rules and controlled documents
summary: Understand the purpose of authorisation levels, safety documents, operational communication, handover and configuration control without substituting generic training for site rules.

title: Isolation as a system condition
summary: Treat isolation as an established electrical condition requiring credible sources, automatic functions and alternative paths to be accounted for.

title: Proving and verification principles
summary: Understand why indication, monitoring and verbal confirmation are not substitutes for the approved means of establishing electrical condition.

title: Stop, challenge and escalate
summary: Practise recognising insufficient, conflicting or unexpected information as a reason to stop and resolve uncertainty.

title: HV distribution architecture
summary: Incoming supplies, switchboards, bus sections, transformer feeders and resilient arrangements.

title: Switchgear families and functions
summary: Differentiate switching, interruption, isolation, earthing and protection functions; recognise AIS, GIS and RMU concepts.

title: Transformer interfaces
summary: Understand transformer purpose, vector/neutral implications at a conceptual level, protection interfaces and the HV/LV operational boundary.

title: Device state and interlocking
summary: Interpret connected, isolated, withdrawn/test states where applicable and understand mechanical/electrical/logical interlock intent.

title: HV/LV backfeed thinking
summary: Challenge the assumption that removal of the normal HV source alone establishes the complete safe condition of connected equipment.

title: Conductors and return paths
summary: Revisit phase, neutral, protective conductors and exposed conductive parts through the question: where can normal and fault current return?

title: Fault families
summary: Distinguish overload, short-circuit and insulation/earth faults and connect each to expected protection behaviour.

title: Protection devices
summary: Fuse, circuit breaker, residual protection, insulation monitoring and electronic trip functions in context.

title: Earthing arrangements
summary: Compare TT, TN-S, TN-C and IT conceptually, focusing on fault-current paths, neutral-earth relationships and operational implications.

title: Sectionalised LV boards
summary: Interpret incomers, bus sections, couplers, outgoing ways, A/B distribution and changed configurations.

title: Multiple infeeds and backfeed
summary: Trace every credible source rather than relying on the normal supply path.

title: Breaking and withstand capability
summary: Introduce prospective fault current and Icu/Ics/Icw/Icm as equipment-selection and operational-awareness concepts.

title: Trip units and selectivity
summary: Develop LSIG, time/current coordination and selective fault clearance conceptually; settings remain study- and equipment-specific.

title: Why critical loads use UPS
summary: Continuity, power conditioning and ride-through in mission-critical architecture.

title: Double-conversion path
summary: Follow AC input through rectification, DC link and inversion to the critical load.

title: DC link and capacitors
summary: Understand stored electrical energy, discharge behaviour and why de-energised AC does not automatically mean absence of hazardous energy.

title: Battery as an independent source
summary: Treat battery strings as sources with their own isolation, stored energy and DC-specific hazards.

title: Static bypass
summary: Understand the alternative electronic path, source compatibility and its effect on the list of credible energisation paths.

title: Maintenance bypass
summary: Understand why a maintenance path changes the operational architecture and can place the load outside the normal power-conversion route.

title: UPS operating states
summary: Recognise normal conversion, battery operation, bypass states, reduced redundancy and unavailable equipment.

title: Parallel UPS and load sharing
summary: Understand redundancy, parallel modules and load distribution without assuming vendor-specific control behaviour.

title: Capacity and residual load
summary: Use simplified capacity exercises to judge whether removing equipment consumes redundancy or leaves adequate headroom.

title: UPS isolation reasoning
summary: Use fictional diagrams to identify sources, stored energy, bypass paths and missing information; never substitute the exercise for an approved site procedure.

title: Two sources, one load
summary: Establish preferred and alternative source concepts.

title: Synchronisation fundamentals
summary: Voltage magnitude, frequency, phase sequence and phase relationship as prerequisites for controlled paralleling.

title: Open and controlled-overlap transfer
summary: Compare break-before-make with design-specific controlled parallel transfer.

title: ATS operation
summary: Understand monitored source health, transfer logic, automatic/manual states and failure modes conceptually.

title: STS operation
summary: Understand rapid static transfer between compatible sources and its role in critical distribution.

title: Bus coupling
summary: Explore how couplers alter energisation paths, fault levels, redundancy and operational boundaries.

title: Abnormal transfer states
summary: Incomplete transfer, failed transfer, unexpected source, inhibited automation and contradictory indication.

title: Mechanical criticality
summary: Why cooling, pumps, air movement and controls are part of electrical operational risk.

title: Motor and drive supplies
summary: Conceptual motor, VFD and control-power relationships.

title: Redundant mechanical trains
summary: How A/B or duty/standby arrangements interact with electrical resilience.

title: ATS-fed mechanical loads
summary: Trace normal and alternate supplies to critical mechanical equipment.

title: Control and auxiliary power
summary: Recognise that loss of control power can change equipment behaviour even where main power remains.

title: Operational consequence mapping
summary: State what facility capability is lost or degraded when a feeder or board changes state.

title: Construction to operational state
summary: Differentiate design intent, as-built state, commissioning state and final operational state.

title: Progressive energisation
summary: Understand staged introduction of energy and controlled handover at a conceptual level.

title: Temporary configurations
summary: Account for temporary supplies, cables, test equipment, inhibited automation and unavailable plant.

title: Load-bank principles
summary: Understand why artificial load is used, what system behaviour is observed and why temporary connections change the safety picture.

title: Transfer and resilience testing
summary: Understand the purpose of loaded transfer and resilience proving without embedding a generic switching sequence.

title: Integrated Systems Testing
summary: Relate electrical, UPS, transfer and mechanical responses during integrated proving.

title: Restoration and configuration control
summary: Verify that temporary arrangements are accounted for and the intended system state is positively re-established.

title: Prospective fault current
summary: Understand how source impedance and configuration influence fault magnitude.

title: Selectivity and discrimination
summary: Understand why the nearest appropriate protective device should clear a fault while preserving healthy distribution where the design permits.

title: Zone selective interlocking
summary: Learn the coordination concept without assuming a universal vendor implementation.

title: Same fault, different source
summary: Compare the implications of transformer/mains, UPS inverter, bypass and alternate-source feeding; use approved studies/manufacturer data for actual performance.

title: Harmonics and THD
summary: Understand non-linear loads, current distortion and resulting voltage distortion as operational-awareness concepts.

title: Neutral and thermal effects
summary: Explore phase imbalance, triplen harmonics and heating as possible symptoms requiring investigation.

title: Voltage and frequency disturbances
summary: Recognise sags, interruptions, transients and source-quality issues.

title: Abnormal system states
summary: Unexpected trips, failed transfer, reduced redundancy, contradictory indication, interlock conflict, control-power failure and temporary-configuration conflict.

title: Restoration reasoning
summary: Reconstruct actual state, identify what changed and establish what information is needed before a controlled return to intended configuration.

title: Whole-system reconstruction
summary: Rebuild the current configuration from a fictional SLD, equipment states and operational information.

title: Energy-source challenge
summary: Identify normal, alternative, stored and automatic sources plus unresolved information.

title: Operational-boundary challenge
summary: Explain the conceptual safety boundary and challenge assumptions.

title: Resilience and consequence
summary: Identify lost redundancy and downstream consequences.

title: Abnormal-event analysis
summary: Separate known facts from assumptions and identify the next information needed.

title: Integrated mock assessment
summary: Multi-part assessment across knowledge, diagram interpretation, scenario judgement and evidence review.

title: Assessment readiness
summary: Course completion is not authorisation; readiness requires defined knowledge, scenario, evidence, mentor and AE gates.
